skill.name: validating-resources
skill.description: Review the complete configured resource set against portable policy, current schema, record shape, bounded liveness, and cross-record evidence with explicit coverage. Use for a full resource-governance sweep; do not use for one known edit, schema-document drift, or resource capture.
skill.shortDescription: Produce an evidence-backed resource drift report with explicit coverage.
skill.defaultPrompt: Use $validating-resources to review the complete configured resource set and distinguish checked, skipped, unknown, adjacent, and fixable findings.

instructions: Resolve the exact resource policy, portable record model, selected provider mapping, current provider schema, configured resource scope, and active lock before reviewing records.
Compare the policy field declarations, portable Context meaning, and observed mapped schema without silently adapting one to another.
Treat every mismatch as a visible finding and keep provider-specific workspace identifiers out of the provider-neutral guide.
stopConditions: Stop when the governed policy, mapping, schema, configured population, or exact current lock is missing or ambiguous.

instructions: Review every configured record against naming, permitted options, required fields, administrator requirements, no-secret rules, and the declared body contract.
Scan the complete governed body representation rather than only mapped properties or templated sections.
Preserve allowed hand-written content while reporting duplicated template regions, unexplained credential-like material, and stale access references.
flexibility: An as-applicable section may be absent when the owning policy explicitly permits its absence.
stopConditions: Stop the complete-sweep claim when any configured record or required governed surface was not available for review.

instructions: Resolve administrator identities through the configured authority and distinguish an explicitly documented external contact from an unexplained unresolved identity.
Perform bounded URL reachability or liveness checks and record redirects, authentication limits, and unavailable observations exactly.
Validate declared cross-record relationships in both directions using portable identities and the selected integration mappings.
flexibility: For authentication-gated locations, report the exact reachability boundary rather than claiming content validity.
stopConditions: Stop before a reality claim when its required authority, capability, evidence source, or freshness cannot be established.

instructions: Partition every configured record and every required check into checked, skipped, unavailable, or adjacent coverage with stable reason codes.
Group findings as policy-to-schema, record-to-policy, record-to-reality, and adjacent-system responsibility.
Never turn a sample, time-bounded subset, failed observation, or unsupported check into a complete-sweep result.
flexibility: A partial review may still be useful when its exact scope and omissions remain explicit.
stopConditions: Stop the complete status unless represented and excluded coverage reconciles to the exact configured population and required check set.

instructions: Prepare only changes directly supported by fresh evidence and identify each missing human-owned fact as a required input rather than guessing it.
Bind every candidate fix to the exact record, before fingerprint, proposed fingerprint, mapping, authority, verification criterion, and selected subset.
Keep private before and proposed values in selected-work review material and expose only sanitized fingerprints through general inspection.
flexibility: Several independent fixes may share one review only when each operation remains separately itemized and subset-bound.
stopConditions: Stop before approval when a fix needs an unavailable fact, unsupported capability, or unverified provider translation.

instructions: Create an expiring exact-scope request for the selected fix subset, record exact confirmation separately, and consume it once into a durable checkpoint before effects.
Apply and verify each selected change through the current capability route, stopping on the first ambiguous write or failed verification.
Stamp any validation date only when the operator explicitly confirms that record as verified, then close with the remaining required-input worklist.
stopConditions: Stop and reconcile when any selected effect, read-after-write observation, or preservation invariant cannot be proven exactly.

verification: The exact policy, Context model, provider mapping, schema, configured population, and lock are current.
Coverage reconciles every configured record and required check without a silent sample or omission.
Each finding names its evidence, freshness, responsible system, and any unavailable observation.
Every proposed fix is exact, private-reviewable, independently selectable, and free of guessed facts.
Applied fixes are re-read from a newer observation and all declared preservation requirements pass.

gotchas.summary: A policy-shaped sweep can look complete while omitting URL liveness or cross-record reality checks.
gotchas.countermeasure: Reconcile every required check into checked, skipped, unavailable, or adjacent coverage before stating completeness.

gotchas.summary: A request to fix everything can pressure the workflow to invent missing administrators, classifications, or links.
gotchas.countermeasure: Prepare only evidence-backed changes and leave every missing human-owned fact as an explicit required input.

gotchas.summary: Pre-template freeform content can retain expired access material or duplicate governed facts outside mapped fields.
gotchas.countermeasure: Review the entire governed body representation and preserve a distinct finding for every stale or unexplained access reference.

gotchas.summary: An unresolved administrator identity can be intentional when the record explicitly documents an external contact.
gotchas.countermeasure: Treat unresolved plus unexplained as drift and retain documented external administration as an explicit observed condition.

limitations: This guide provides procedural guidance only and grants no worker dispatch, file-write, publication, provider, merge, or host-realization authority.
Behavior evidence requires an exact private request and an independently observed fresh-worker run through a trusted host boundary.
